text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- European Commission to reinvestigate Finland's tax relief on xylitol which it currently plans to ban as a hidden subsidy, Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen says.
- Destruction of forests has continued this decade, with forest areas declining rapidly in third world countries and growing much less in the developed world.
- Increasing amounts of hand luggage are becoming a risk to flight security, airlines say.
- A 61-year-old man who was attacked by a northern Lunx may be charged with a hunting violation for killing the beast.
- Helsinki planning recreational area with an artificial river with for fishing, canoeing and more.
- Forest industry group Enso planning to up pulp prices in May-June, Enso official says but declines to say by how much.
- Helsinki's Jokerit wins its fourth ice-hockey championship in six years, beating Turku's Turun Palloseura 4-0 in third and decisive leg of finals.
KAUPPALEHTI
- U.S. pulp producers Georgia-Pacific and Stone are planning to raise pulp prices to $580 per tonne from $520 in May.
- UK-owned petrol distributor Station 1 entering Finnish market, managing director says.
- New commercial television station Ruutunelonen has so far made programme contracts for tens of millions but less than 100 million markka, managing director says.
AAMULEHTI
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says he is in good health according to a recent examination.
- Wood heating is gaining in popularity in Pirkanmaa due to high oil prices, and many municipalities are planning to build chip power plants.
- Combined freight-passenger Ro-Ro ships have are becoming increasingly common in the Baltic Sea.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnish markka bills are difficult to forge, Bank of Finland official says.
- State railways to decide this autumn whether to use its option to buy eight Italian Pendolino trains after test use.
